method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Magistrates Court Act 2004 (WA) (No. 47 of 2004), compilation as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_47672.txt (legislation.wa.gov.au mrdoc 47672, retrieved 2026-09-07); contempt maximum $12 000 or 12 months in the Act itself (s 16(4)); 'written law' read with the Interpretation Act 1984 s 5 as deposited; no regulations or rules of court used (not deposited): when JPs may constitute the Court (s 7(2)) and what is delegated to registrars (s 28(1)) are inputs
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is reproduced under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution in ../../SOURCE-LICENSE.md

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: s 7(1), (2), (4), (6) (who constitutes the Court; a bench of JPs), s 8(1)(c), (2) (where it may sit), ss 9, 10 (where its jurisdiction comes from: the Civil Proceedings Act, another WA written law, or a Commonwealth law outside s 9's words), s 14 (rules of evidence), s 16(4) (contempt maxima), s 17 (a claim refused as frivolous or vexatious), s 23(1) (slips), s 28(1)(b), (c) and s 29 (registrars; appeal to a magistrate within 21 days), s 30 (self-represented party), s 33(3), (4), (8), (11)(a) (records). The civil limits, excluded claims and minor cases procedure are in the Magistrates Court (Civil Proceedings) Act 2004 baseline and are not repeated. Out: criminal jurisdiction (ss 11, 11A), magistrates' appointment (ss 5, 6, Schs 1-3), ss 15, 18-22, 31, 32, 34-37, Part 4 save ss 28-29, ss 38-42.
lives: jake k062 (2036-03-10): the Fair Work Ombudsman, then a small claim in the Magistrates Court; judgment for $4,100
